faqs.question: What is the Solar Simulator used for?
faqs.answer: It's a xenon-based light source built to match the ASTM G173 AM1.5 solar spectrum, used for sunscreen testing, photobiology, photodegradation studies, and pharmaceutical photostability testing.

faqs.question: How do I know my simulator is actually matching the AM1.5 spectrum?
faqs.answer: The included calibrated Sunmeter measures and confirms the AM1.5 match directly, rather than relying on the filter set alone.

faqs.question: Does this system need ventilation?
faqs.answer: No, the ozone-free xenon design removes that requirement for the lamp itself; ventilation is only needed if your own experimental byproducts call for it.

faqs.question: What's the difference between SolSim2, LZCX-ICH1, and LZCX-Xe?
faqs.answer: SolSim2 handles general AM1.5 solar simulation, LZCX-ICH1 carries ICH Option 1 certification for pharmaceutical photostability testing, and LZCX-Xe opens the same platform to your own custom filters.

faqs.question: How do I choose between a xenon-based system and LED-SOL?
faqs.answer: Choose a Xenon Series configuration if your work needs UV coverage; choose LED-SOL if your application stays in the visible and near-infrared range, such as photovoltaic or energy research.

faqs.question: Is this system certified for pharmaceutical stability testing?
faqs.answer: The LZCX-ICH1 configuration is certified for ICH Option 1 photostability testing specifically; confirm this configuration if your protocol requires that certification.

faqs.question: What wavelength range does the Solar Simulator cover?
faqs.answer: 300 to 800nm is the confirmed spectral interval for standard AM1.5 matching; the underlying xenon platform can extend further depending on configuration and filters chosen.

faqs.question: What power does the xenon lamp run at?
faqs.answer: 300W with variable output power, adjustable to match your specific irradiance protocol.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Solar Simulator in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote around your Xenon Series configuration or LED-SOL selection.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Solar Simulator in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Luzchem Solar Simulator range in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.subheading: Why matching a named reference standard matters
body: Simulating sunlight well means being able to say exactly which reference standard your output matches, and SolSim2 is built to match ASTM G173, the AM1.5 solar spectrum most commonly cited in photostability and solar-driven research, across the 300 to 800 nm range.

The design runs ozone-free, which removes the mandatory ventilation requirement that standard ozone-generating xenon lamps carry, useful in labs without dedicated exhaust infrastructure already in place. A 300W xenon lamp with variable output power sits at the core, paired with the complete filter set needed to hold that AM1.5 match and a calibrated Sunmeter for confirming it's holding.

The same Xenon Series platform underneath SolSim2 also configures two other ways. LZCX-ICH1 carries certification for ICH Option 1 pharmaceutical photostability testing specifically, and LZCX-Xe opens the system up to your own custom filters for general photochemical research.

sections.title: AM1.5 Solar Spectrum Matching and Ozone-Free Design
sections.description: Matching a named standard rather than an approximate "sunlight-like" output is what separates a real solar simulator from a bright broadband lamp. ASTM G173 defines the AM1.5 solar spectrum, and the filter set included with every Xenon Series unit is what holds output to that spectrum across the confirmed 300-800nm interval. The ozone-free build removes a real practical burden most xenon-based systems carry. Standard ozone-generating xenon lamps require dedicated ventilation because of the ozone they produce as a byproduct; this design doesn't generate that ozone in the first place, so ventilation only becomes necessary if your own experiment's byproducts require it, not because of the light source itself.

sections.eyebrow: Configurations and the broader solar range
sections.title: Xenon Series Configurations and the Broader Solar Range
sections.description: One xenon platform underneath three configurations means the right choice depends entirely on what you're testing against, not the hardware itself. SolSim2 is built for general controlled sunlight simulation. LZCX-ICH1 carries ICH Option 1 certification specifically, relevant if your photostability testing needs to meet that pharmaceutical standard directly rather than approximate it. LZCX-Xe opens the same core system to your own custom filters, useful when your research needs a spectral profile the standard AM1.5 filter set doesn't provide.
body: A separate LED-based system, LED-SOL, sits in the broader Solar range alongside the Xenon Series. It's AAA compliant and meets IEC60904-9 spectral, spatial, and temporal requirements, but covers visible and near-infrared only, not the UV range the xenon-based systems reach, making it suited specifically to energy and photovoltaic research rather than UV-dependent photostability work.
